inputs.share_count_basis: 932.5M, diluted = basic per Q2 2026 interim EPS note (BCE.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:3395-3397). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 2.2% count growth in FY2025 (912.3M -> 932.5M) was discounted-DRIP share issuance, non-SBC; it stopped after Q3 2025 (count flat Q3 FY2025 through Q2 FY2026) alongside the dividend reset, so no forward non-SBC issuance is modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, statement of cash flows share-based payments add-back (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 = 90; FY2022-25 range 84-101). Equity-award cash taxes disclosed nil (Metrics.csv EquityAwardTaxes = 0). BCE settles most LTIP awards in cash/DSUs, which is why the SBC line is only ~0.4% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows. GoC 10-year ~3.3%, ERP 5.0%, levered beta 0.85 (BCE's raw beta is ~0.6 but the equity sits under 3.7x net debt/EBITDA) -> cost of equity ~7.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (2025-26 Bell Canada issuance priced 4.6-5.3%, hybrids 6.875%), after-tax 3.7% at 26.5%. At the company's own 3.0x target structure (~50/50 debt/equity at market) the mechanical WACC is ~5.6%; the house rate is 6.5%, adding ~0.9pp for an equity claim that is ~38% of enterprise value under BBB/Baa2 ratings that rely on hybrid and preferred equity credit. Held constant across bear/base/bull: scenario risk is charged in the driver paths and the 30/50/20 weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease cash cost = principal 1,127 (financing CF, BCE.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:4543) + interest on lease liabilities 194 (note 9480) = 1,321 = 5.4% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (glides to 4.5%: 2025 lease terminations of 724 cost shrank the base and H1 2026 principal ran 499 vs 582, partly offset by Ziply leases). D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: 5,238 - 874 ROU depreciation (note 19) = 4,364 = 17.8% of revenue. Lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt: total_debt 37,576 = Q2 2026 long-term debt 37,522 + debt due within one year 4,254 = 41,776, less lease liabilities estimated at ~4,200 (Dec-2025 balance 4,309 per note 24; the Q2 2026 interim does not break the balance out but states lease liabilities fell over H1; +/-200 on this estimate moves value by ~$0.21/share).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI share of earnings is ~1% of net income); the NCI book value of 314 at 30 Jun 2026 (BCE.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:2877) is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row: operating company, non-US, with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied for leases, NCI, preferred capital and a CAD WACC). BCE is a regulated-oligopoly telecom operating company; a bank/REIT/LIC model does not apply. BASE YEAR: FY2025 revenue 24,468 and adjusted EBITDA 10,658 (43.6%). FY2025 reported net income of 6,305 includes a ~5.2bn pre-tax MLSE gain and FY2024's 163 carries a 2,190 impairment; neither is a base, which is why the build runs off adjusted EBITDA and the component margin, consistent with how BCE itself guides. OWNER EBITDA: the adjusted margin is haircut by ~0.8pp for recurring severance/acquisition/other costs (FY2022-25: 94, 200, 454, 517; avg 1.3% of revenue; the $1.5bn cost program through 2028 means this line does not go to zero). CAPITAL STRUCTURE: junior subordinated hybrid notes (5,892 at Q2 2026; rating agencies give 50% equity credit) are held at 100% debt because they are interest-bearing contractual claims ahead of common. First Preferred Shares of 3,216 (30 Jun 2026) and NCI of 314 are deducted in the equity bridge; preferred dividends (~170/yr) are not in the unlevered flows so this charges them exactly once. INTEREST INCOME: 79 in FY2025 is not stripped; the company is a large net debtor and cash of 479 is netted in net debt. The ~$0.5bn MLSE cash tax was paid in Q1 2026 (547 cash taxes) and is already in the 30 Jun 2026 net debt. PENDING DISPOSALS (Northwestel up to $1bn; land mobile radio business $675m) are left inside the operating flows and not added to the bridge: they are roughly value-neutral swaps of EBITDA for debt reduction. Pension surplus (~$4.4bn solvency) is trapped and not added; its contribution holiday is already in the flows. last_fcf is owner FCF on the company's FCF basis (OCF - capex - SBC = 3,293 - 90), which is levered and pre-lease-principal; the projection is the unlevered, lease-charged component build and is not comparable to last_fcf one-for-one (FY2025 unlevered owner FCF on the component basis is ~3,870 after the severance haircut). Working capital: receivables + inventory roughly offset payables and deferred revenue at a ~1%-growth telecom; wc_capture 0.

equity_bridge.item: First Preferred Shares (senior to common; dividends not in unlevered flows)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance midpoint (revenue +1% to +5%, carrying 7 incremental months of Ziply Fiber and FIFA 2026 media revenue) tapering to the 5-year revenue CAGR of ~1.4% by year 4; the revenue series is the only clean one.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs use ADJUSTED EPS (FY2020 3.02, FY2022 3.35, FY2025 ~2.80); reported EPS (2.98 -> 6.79) is distorted by the FY2025 MLSE gain and FY2024 impairment. Equity CAGR is likewise distorted by those two items. Adjusted EPS fell ~5.8%/yr over 3 years while revenue grew 0.4%/yr: the divergence is interest expense (1,146 -> 1,775) and D&A (4,723 -> 5,238) outrunning EBITDA, i.e. leverage and the capex cycle, not the operating margin (which rose to a 30-year high).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported OCF - capex - SBC): FY2020 3,461, FY2022 3,131, FY2025 3,203. SBC is ~0.4% of revenue and flat, so the owner and reported series move together; the SBC adjustment is immaterial here and the CAGR gap is entirely the capex cycle (capex 4,202 -> 5,133 -> 3,700). Pre-2019 figures are pre-IFRS 16 and not comparable; the 5-year window starts at FY2020 deliberately.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at 3.0%, the midpoint of the 1-5% guide, carried by the extra 7 months of Ziply, FIFA 2026 at Bell Media and wireless subscriber recovery; H1 2026 ran +2.7%. Thereafter 2% then 1.5%: a mature oligopoly with ARPU pressure, Media legacy decline and ~1% population growth, with Ziply/fibre adding ~0.5pp.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 adjusted margin 43.6% less a 0.8pp recurring severance/restructuring charge = 42.8% owner margin in FY2026 (guide: EBITDA 0-4% vs revenue 1-5%, i.e. roughly flat adjusted margin; H1 2026 +1.9% EBITDA on +2.7% revenue). The $1.5bn cost program lifts the adjusted margin to ~44.3% by 2029-30, net of the recurring charge 43.5%.
base.capex_rationale: Capital intensity 15.1% in FY2025, guided <15% in FY2026 (capex ~3.7bn flat on higher revenue) as Canadian FTTP spend declines and is partly reallocated to Ziply; glides to 13.5% by 2032 as the fibre build completes. BCE's own three-year framework implies ~15% FCF-after-leases CAGR to 2028 off falling intensity.
base.da_rationale: D&A ex right-of-use is 17.8% of revenue vs 15.1% capex, the lag of a decade of heavy fibre/5G and spectrum-related amortisation; it converges toward capex + 0.5pp by the terminal year so the terminal tax shield is not larger than the capex that sustains it.
base.tax_rationale: Canadian combined statutory ~26.5%; cash taxes have run below provision on accelerated CCA (FY2025 cash 737 on levered pre-tax ~2,750 = 26.8% levered, but unlevered EBIT taxed at 26.5% would be higher). Start at 25% for residual CCA timing and ramp to 26.5% by year 4. Ziply's US income is small and roughly tax-neutral.
base.terminal_rationale: Terminal cap of 15x unlevered owner FCF binds (Gordon at 6.5%/2.0% implies 22.7x). 15x is roughly today's ex-lease EV / FY2025 unlevered owner FCF (~65.6bn / ~3.9bn severance-adjusted, ~15x excluding severance), so no multiple expansion is assumed.

bull.narrative: Top of the FY2026 guide (4.5%), then 3-3.5% as Ziply Fiber and Network FiberCo deliver ~3m US passings by 2028 with penetration ramping, AI-powered enterprise solutions (+60% in FY2025) compound, and Crave/digital more than offset linear Media decline. Cost program delivers in full with severance fading (owner margin to 45.0%). Capex intensity falls to 12.5% as the Canadian build is complete and US build is co-funded by PSP. Leverage reaches 3.0x ahead of 2030; terminal cap 16x, growth 2.5%.

bear.narrative: Bottom of the FY2026 guide (1.0%), then revenue flat-to-down for three years: CRTC wholesale-access and MVNO mandates let resellers ride Bell's fibre and 5G, three-way price competition pushes wireless ARPU below $56 and churn back toward 2%, Bell Media's linear decline outruns Crave, and Starlink erodes Northwestel/rural. Owner EBITDA margin compresses 3pp to 40.5% as cost savings are competed away and severance stays elevated. Capital intensity cannot fall below ~14.6% because the fibre/5G race continues. Leverage stays near 3.7x past 2027; a further dividend cut is plausible but is a distribution decision and does not change enterprise value here. Terminal cap 13x, growth 1.0%.

scenario_narratives.base: Management's three-year framework executed roughly as guided, no better: revenue +3% in FY2026 (Ziply full-year, FIFA, wireless recovery) tapering to 1.5%; adjusted EBITDA margin drifts up ~0.7pp on the $1.5bn cost program while recurring severance absorbs ~0.8pp; capex intensity falls from 15.1% to 13.5% as the Canadian fibre build completes; leverage reaches 3.5x by end-2027 and ~3.0x by 2030 from FCF, Northwestel and LMR proceeds; the dividend is held at $1.75 then grows slowly within the 40-55% payout policy. Equity is ~38% of enterprise value, so every 10% change in EV moves the per-share value ~26%: the scenario spread below is leverage, not indecision.
scenario_narratives.bull: US fibre (Ziply + Network FiberCo) becomes a genuine second growth engine, AI enterprise solutions scale, Media digital crosses over, cost program fully lands with severance fading, capex intensity to 12.5%, leverage to 3.0x early. Needs several independent things to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: CRTC wholesale pressure plus competitive intensity compress margins by 3pp, revenue stalls for three years, capital intensity stays ~15% to defend the network, leverage stays elevated past 2027 and the dividend is at risk again. Per-share value falls far below the current price because the debt and preferred stack is fixed.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 30/50/20. Bear up to 30%: net debt/EBITDA of 3.7x after a 56% dividend cut, a single regulator (CRTC) whose wholesale-access rulings directly set the return on BCE's largest asset, and equity that is only ~38% of enterprise value so operating misses are amplified ~2.6x per share. Bull down to 20%: it requires Ziply's US build, the $1.5bn cost program, Media's digital crossover and Canadian wireless pricing discipline to all land together, in a market where adjusted EPS has fallen three years running. Base at 50% because the FY2026 guide is the company's own framework and H1 2026 is tracking it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BCE is valued as an unlevered stream of owner FCF (adjusted EBITDA less recurring severance, SBC and full lease cash cost, less tax on EBIT, less capex) discounted at a CAD WACC of 6.5% with the terminal value capped at 15x FCF (no multiple expansion), from which Q2 2026 net debt (ex-lease, hybrids at 100%), preferred shares and NCI are deducted. Reported net income is ignored as a base: FY2025 carries the MLSE gain and FY2024 an impairment. The dividend is a distribution decision and does not enter the value; what matters is whether FCF after leases, interest and preferred dividends covers deleveraging to 3.0x. The valuation is a leveraged bet on a slow-growth regulated utility-like cash flow: the scenario spread is wide because 62% of enterprise value is fixed claims.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage amplification: equity is ~38% of EV, so a 10% miss on terminal EBITDA or a 1x lower exit multiple is ~25-30% off the per-share value.
CRTC wholesale-access and MVNO rulings directly reduce the return on BCE's fibre and spectrum and can also lower long-run capex intensity less than assumed.
Terminal cap multiple: the 15x cap is the binding terminal assumption in every scenario; at 13x the base case loses ~$6/share, at 17x it gains ~$6.
WACC: a CAD build at target leverage is ~5.6%; the house 6.5% embeds ~0.9pp of leverage premium. At 6.0% base value rises ~$5/share, at 7.0% it falls ~$4.
Lease-liability estimate at 30 Jun 2026 (~4,200) is inferred from the Dec-2025 balance and H1 principal payments; the interim does not disclose it.
Ziply Fiber integration, US regulatory exposure and USD/CAD translation are new to BCE; the base case gives them only ~0.5pp of growth.
Bell Media's linear decline and content costs (NHL/NBA rights through 2043-44 retained at MLSE sale) could compress the group margin faster than cost savings arrive.
Pending Northwestel and LMR disposals are assumed value-neutral (EBITDA out, debt down); a shortfall versus book would be a small negative.
